hints: The flight arrival outcomes on any day are early ($0.15$), on time ($0.55$), and late ($0.3$).
Find the probability that the flight does not arrive late on a single day: $1 - 0.3 = 0.7$ (or $0.15 + 0.55 = 0.7$).
Because the arrival status on different days is independent, multiply the single-day probability across 3 days: $(0.7)^3$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the probability that the flight does not arrive late on any single day using the complement rule:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{not late}) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(\text{late}) = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7$$

For 3 independent days, multiply the probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{not late on all 3 days}) = (0.7)^3 = 0.343$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the single-day probability of not arriving late.
On any given day, the flight can arrive early (probability $0.15$), on time (probability $0.55$), or late (probability $0.30$).
The event 'does not arrive late' means arriving early or on time:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{not late}) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(\text{late}) = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7$$
(Equivalently, $0.15 + 0.55 = 0.7$).

Step 2: Apply independence across 3 days.
Assuming the flight arrivals on 3 randomly chosen days are mutually independent events:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{not late on Day 1 and Day 2 and Day 3}) = \mathrm{P}(\text{not late})^3 = (0.7)^3$$
Calculate the power:
$$(0.7)^3 = 0.7 \times 0.7 \times 0.7 = 0.49 \times 0.7 = 0.343$$

hints: Define the random variable $Y$ as the number of days the flight arrives early out of $n = 9$ days. Since the probability of arriving early is $p = 0.15$, $Y \sim B(9, 0.15)$.
We want the probability of arriving early at least 3 times: $\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 3)$.
Evaluate each binomial probability using $\binom{9}{y} (0.15)^y (0.85)^{9-y}$, sum them, subtract from 1, and round to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Define the binomial model for the number of early arrivals $Y$ in 9 days:
$$Y \sim B(9, 0.15)$$

Sum the lower tail terms and subtract from 1:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \le 2) = 0.231617 + 0.367862 + 0.259668 = 0.859147$$
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 3) = 1 - 0.859147 = 0.140853 \approx 0.141$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up the binomial distribution.
Let $Y$ be the number of days the flight arrives early out of $n = 9$ independent days. The probability of arriving early on any single day is $p = 0.15$, so the probability of not arriving early is $q = 1 - p = 0.85$:
$$Y \sim B(n, p) = B(9, 0.15)$$

Step 2: Express the required event using the complement.
We need the probability that the flight arrives early at least 3 times, which is $Y \ge 3$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 3) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(Y < 3) = 1 - [\mathrm{P}(Y = 0) + \mathrm{P}(Y = 1) + \mathrm{P}(Y = 2)]$$

Step 4: Sum the lower tail probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \le 2) = 0.23161687 + 0.36786221 + 0.25966744 = 0.85914652$$

Step 5: Subtract from 1:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 3) = 1 - 0.85914652 = 0.14085348$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.141$.

ai_rubric.Calculating Binomial Tail Probabilities: Uses 1 - [P(0) + P(1) + P(2)] with B(9, 0.15) to obtain 0.141.

hints: For $n = 60$ and $p = 0.15$, verify that a normal approximation is appropriate: $np = 9 > 5$ and $n(1 - p) = 51 > 5$.
Calculate the mean and variance: $\mu = np = 60 \times 0.15 = 9$ and $\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 60 \times 0.15 \times 0.85 = 7.65$.
Apply the continuity correction to the inequality $Y \ge 12$: on the continuous scale, this becomes $W > 11.5$.
Standardise $z = \dfrac{11.5 - 9}{\sqrt{7.65}}$, evaluate $1 - \Phi(z)$, and give your answer to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Calculate the parameters of the approximating normal distribution for $Y \sim B(60, 0.15)$:
$$\mu = np = 60 \times 0.15 = 9$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 60 \times 0.15 \times 0.85 = 7.65 \implies \sigma = \sqrt{7.65} \approx 2.7659$$

Apply the continuity correction for the discrete condition 'at least 12':
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 12) \approx \mathrm{P}(W > 11.5)$$

Evaluate the upper tail probability using the standard normal distribution function $\Phi$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.9039) = 1 - \Phi(0.9039)$$
$$\Phi(0.904) \approx 0.8170$$
$$1 - 0.8170 = 0.183$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Check conditions and compute approximating normal parameters.
With $n = 60$ days and early arrival probability $p = 0.15$:
$$np = 60 \times 0.15 = 9 > 5$$
$$n(1 - p) = 60 \times 0.85 = 51 > 5$$
Both conditions are satisfied, so we approximate the discrete variable $Y \sim B(60, 0.15)$ with a continuous normal variable $W \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$:
$$\mu = np = 9$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 60 \times 0.15 \times 0.85 = 7.65$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{7.65} \approx 2.765863$$

Step 2: Apply the continuity correction.
We require the probability that the flight arrives early at least 12 times:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 12)$$
Since $Y$ takes integer values, the discrete integer 12 occupies the continuous interval $[11.5, 12.5]$. To include 12 and all values greater than 12, the continuous boundary starts at $11.5$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y \ge 12) \approx \mathrm{P}(W > 11.5)$$

Step 4: Look up the probability in the standard normal table:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.904) = 1 - \Phi(0.904)$$
From the Cambridge normal distribution tables:
$$\Phi(0.90) = 0.8159$$
The difference for the next digit $4$ is $+11$ (or $0.0011$):
$$\Phi(0.904) = 0.8159 + 0.0011 = 0.8170$$
Subtract from 1:
$$1 - 0.8170 = 0.1830$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.183$.

ai_rubric.Applying a Normal Approximation: Uses mean = 9, variance = 7.65, continuity correction 11.5 to get z = (11.5-9)/sqrt(7.65) = 0.904 and 1 - Phi(0.904) = 0.183.
